note: Simplified view inferred from the project's file structure and database schema. Component names match real folders and files; flows are condensed to their main steps.

nodes.title: Browser
nodes.summary: Members, church admins and the super admin use the system through server-rendered pages in the browser.
details: Pages are generated by PHP on the server and styled with the project's own CSS.
Small JavaScript files handle interface details such as adjusting and viewing photos.

nodes.title: Public & member pages
nodes.summary: One PHP script per page for the public site and member features: events, sacraments, catechesis, pastoral care and donations.
details: Each feature has its own entry page, for example events.php, sacrament-apply.php and donations.php.
Members can follow the status of their requests, for example sacrament-status.php and pastoral-status.php.

nodes.title: Admin dashboards
nodes.summary: Separate dashboards for church admins (one parish) and the super admin (all churches).
details: Church admins manage their own church's announcements, events, sacraments, catechesis, pastoral care and donations.
The super admin manages churches, admin accounts and system-wide statistics.

nodes.title: Authentication & security
nodes.summary: Shared checks that sign users in, enforce roles and protect forms.
details: Passwords are stored with PHP's password_hash and checked with password_verify.
Admin access is split into two roles in the database: super_admin and church_admin.
Forms use CSRF tokens, and output is escaped with htmlspecialchars.
Password-reset, invitation and email-verification tokens are stored as hashes with expiry times.

nodes.title: Shared modules
nodes.summary: Reusable helpers that keep the business rules for each feature in one place.
details: One helper file per feature area, for example sacrament_helpers.php, donation_helpers.php and event_helpers.php.
Shared layout and form rendering keep pages consistent.

nodes.title: Data access (PDO)
nodes.summary: All database access goes through PDO prepared statements.
details: The codebase contains around 295 prepare() calls, so user input is passed as parameters instead of being concatenated into SQL.
files: config/db.php (credentials kept out of this portfolio)

nodes.title: MySQL database
nodes.summary: 22 tables across 9 feature areas, linked by foreign keys.
details: Status workflows such as sacrament applications and donations are stored as ENUM columns.
Explore every table in the Data Model Explorer.

nodes.title: File storage
nodes.summary: Uploaded files such as donation receipts, bulletins and photos are stored on the server; the database keeps their file names.
details: For example, donations.receipt_file and bulletins.file_name point to stored files.

nodes.title: Email (PHPMailer)
nodes.summary: Sends account, announcement, donation and event emails.
details: Covers email verification, password resets, announcement notifications to subscribers, donation updates and event reminders.
Timestamps such as announcements.notified_at and event_registrations.reminded_at record when emails were sent.

nodes.title: Gemini API
nodes.summary: Powers the AI assistant and AI help for writing announcements.
details: Requests are made from the server, so the API key never reaches the browser.

steps.text: A signed-in member fills in the sacrament application form.
sacrament-apply.php receives the form.
The session and CSRF token are checked.
Supporting documents are saved to file storage.
A prepared statement saves the application.
A row is stored in sacrament_applications with its status.
A church admin opens the donation review page.
donation-review.php lists pending donations for their church.
The church_admin role is checked.
The decision is saved with a prepared statement.
donations.status changes to approved or rejected, with reviewed_by and reviewed_at.
The donor is emailed, and email_sent_at is recorded.
A church admin writes an announcement.
Optionally, Gemini helps draft the text.
The announcement is saved.
A row is stored in announcements for that church.
Subscribers in newsletter_subscribers are notified, and notified_at is set.
The user requests a reset on forgot-password.php.
A random token is created and only its hash is kept.
password_resets stores token_hash and expires_at.
A reset link is emailed to the user.
reset-password.php checks the token and its expiry, then saves the new password hash.
